high_stakes_two_source_rule: NOT ENGAGED, and this packet's earlier claim that it was engaged was the error that made the rest of this section necessary. The contract's high-stakes gate covers facts where being wrong changes a user's clinical interpretation - allele direction, risk-allele identity, a metabolizer call, a shipped threshold. WHICH SPELLING NAMES THE SNP IS NOT ONE OF THOSE. No genotype call, category, evidence level or effect claim depends on it; the change is a rendered string. Marking it high-stakes invited a gate that then could not be met, and two attempts to satisfy it named sources that were not independent (Ensembl, which imports variants from dbSNP; UniProt P41440, which cross-references the very RefSeq records dbSNP reports against). THE HIGH-STAKES FACT AT THIS LOCUS IS THE DIRECTION OF EFFECT - which allele reduces folate transport - and that IS contested, IS withheld, and IS filed separately. This change does not touch it: risk_allele, ref_allele, every genotype_effects category and the evidence level are unchanged, and the effect prose was softened rather than sharpened. Independent of the gate, the change asserts no new fact either: hgvs_protein 'p.His27Arg' was already in the row, agrees with the committed tests/fixtures/seed_csvs/vep_seed.csv, and matches every database consulted. The change conforms the single outlier field to a claim the row already made, and the guard it adds enforces internal consistency, which is frame-independent.

queries.derived_extract_rule: Retains identity, merge status and every NM_194255.4 placement with its NP_919231.1 protein consequence. Kept for readability only; the source-native 250974-byte response is retained in full alongside it, so any selection or transcription can be checked.
queries.result_used: rs1051266 is not merged. NM_194255.4:c.80= maps to NP_919231.1 residue 27 H->H, establishing His as the reference residue; NM_194255.4:c.80A>G maps to residue 27 H->R as a missense_variant. The same transcript also carries c.80A>C (H->P) and c.80A>T (H->L), so dbSNP records THREE alternates and the record is four-allelic (A reference plus G, C, T). Ensembl's GRCh37 allele_string is narrower at T/C/G, i.e. two alternates; the packet reports both rather than reconciling them. Either way, A>G is one alternate among several and not 'the' alternate.
queries.supports: A80G (His27Arg) is the reference-frame spelling; G80A is not.

corroborating_query.description: Same committed bundle joined against the committed tests/fixtures/seed_csvs/vep_seed.csv on (rsid, pos). The recorded statement matches on (rsid, pos) ALONE; the orientation split below then applies a further filter on the unordered allele pair, which the SQL does not express.

corroborating_query.why_26_are_excluded: Orientation is undefined when the two sources do not name the same two alleles, so those 26 cannot be scored as agreeing or reversed and are counted separately rather than dropped silently. They differ by more than orientation - some are strand complements (rs5026665 seed T/C vs bundle A/G), others name a different alternate entirely (rs913722 seed A/T vs bundle C/T; rs7601387 seed A/T vs bundle A/G). They are a further discrepancy class between the two artifacts and are NOT evidence for the alphabetical-ordering finding, which rests on the 102254/102254 count above.

queries.artifact_transcription_note: The retained artifact is NCBI's gc.prt as retrieved, 16444 bytes, and the SHA-256 above covers those complete bytes - not a digest over extracted strings. The guard parses translation table 1 straight out of this file. tests/fixtures/ncbi_genetic_code_table1.json beside it is a readable extract asserted field-by-field equal to that parse, and is not the authority; an earlier version of this entry pointed at the extract and described a digest over its five strings, which would have sent an auditor to the wrong artifact and the wrong checksum procedure.
queries.result_used: Translation table 1 (Standard), 64 codons; stops TAA/TAG/TGA; starts TTG/CTG/ATG. The guard derives which base substitutions can produce which amino-acid changes from this.
queries.supports: That the genetic code underpinning the new panel-label guard is sourced rather than encoded from memory. The digest is pinned because the code is redundant: corrupting one codon of a multi-codon amino acid changes no reachability result and would otherwise be invisible.

queries.result_used: The three requested accessions - AAA98442.1, AAC50180.1, AAB35058.1 - are each 591 aa with residues 20-35 = PELRSWRRLVCYLCFY, i.e. residue 27 = R (Arg), the OTHER allele from the RefSeq/UniProt canonical His27.
queries.supports: ONLY the sequence fact: that these three accessions carry Arg27. Nothing more. The retained artifact is FASTA - headers and sequence - so it carries no submission dates, submitters, publication links or inter-record relationships, and none were checked. It therefore does NOT establish that these are the earliest submissions, that they were produced independently of one another, or that early authors named the SNP from them. An earlier version of this field asserted all three; that went beyond the evidence and the causal story about the literature's naming remains an unproven inference relied on nowhere. Note also that these records contradict rather than corroborate the reference-residue claim - at MAF about 0.49 a clone carrying either allele is unremarkable, and which allele the assembly adopted is a separate matter.

source_versions_and_licenses._why: Recording the version/build and licence basis for every source, so a future auditor can establish which source state produced each retained payload and on what basis retaining it is permitted.

NCBI dbSNP RefSNP v2.retention_basis: Public domain. Only variant metadata for a single rsID is retained; no human subject data is involved.

UniProtKB P41440.version_or_build: Canonical sequence version 3, read from entryAudit.sequenceVersion in the retained response, pinned further by CRC64 0437B1615F5517EB and MD5 24DE6A075D69E133471E1BC4916E1ED5 over a 591-residue sequence. Accessed 2026-08-10. (accessed 2026-08-10).
UniProtKB P41440.license_or_terms: UniProt data are distributed under CC BY 4.0.
UniProtKB P41440.retention_basis: CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution with attribution, and the source is attributed by accession. Only the canonical protein record is retained.

Ensembl GRCh37 REST.version_or_build: GRCh37 archive endpoint. The response carries no release number, so the 2026-08-10 access date is the retrieval-version boundary. The GRCh37 site is a frozen mirror and lags current dbSNP, which is why dbSNP rather than Ensembl is the primary source for identity and merge status. (accessed 2026-08-10).
Ensembl GRCh37 REST.license_or_terms: Ensembl data are released under the Apache License 2.0.
Ensembl GRCh37 REST.retention_basis: Apache 2.0 permits redistribution with attribution. Only the single-rsID variation record is retained.

Consensus and Scite.version_or_build: Neither service exposes a corpus version; the 2026-08-10 access date is the boundary. (accessed 2026-08-10).
Consensus and Scite.license_or_terms: Only the outcome of each query is retained in prose - which spellings appear in titles/abstracts, and whether an editorial notice exists. No abstract or full text is reproduced beyond short bibliographic identification.

PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.version_or_build: Version of record. These are the three citations already carried by the panel row; only their titles and editorial-notice status are used here. (accessed 2026-08-10).
PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.license_or_terms: Titles only, used as bibliographic fact. No abstract or full text is retained or reproduced.
PMID:16750224 / PMID:24597986 / PMID:339.retention_basis: Bibliographic metadata, attributed by PMID and DOI.

NCBI genetic code table 1.version_or_build: gc.prt version 4.6, as stated in the retained file's own header; the id 1 entry is named 'Standard'. Pinned by SHA-256 2aecbdd09ecc5e0d233c105090a593737298ef93d88f6bc0c1bef26df6051a04 over the complete 16444-byte payload (accessed 2026-08-10).
NCBI genetic code table 1.license_or_terms: US Government work produced by the National Library of Medicine; NCBI data are in the public domain in the United States.
NCBI genetic code table 1.retention_basis: Public domain. The COMPLETE source-native file is retained at tests/fixtures/ncbi_gc.prt - 16444 bytes carrying all 27 translation tables (ids 1 through 33), exactly as NCBI serves it. Nothing was stripped: retaining the file whole is what lets the pinned SHA-256 cover the bytes as retrieved rather than a post-hoc excerpt. The guard parses only the id 1 (Standard) entry from it; the other tables are unused, not removed. An earlier version of this field said only table 1 was retained, which misdescribed both the payload scope and the redistribution basis.

GenBank AAA98442.1 / AAC50180.1 / AAB350.version_or_build: Versioned accessions as retrieved: AAA98442.1, AAC50180.1, AAB35058.1. The trailing .1 is the sequence version, so the record state is pinned by the accession itself; the 2026-08-10 access date bounds retrieval. (accessed 2026-08-10).
GenBank AAA98442.1 / AAC50180.1 / AAB350.license_or_terms: US Government work produced by the National Library of Medicine; GenBank records are in the public domain in the United States. NCBI notes that some submitters may claim patent or other rights in the underlying sequences, which does not restrict redistribution of the records.
GenBank AAA98442.1 / AAC50180.1 / AAB350.retention_basis: Public domain. Only the FASTA protein records for three accessions are retained (raw/genbank-primary-cdna-submissions-2026-08-10.fasta); no annotation, publication text or human subject data is involved. They are retained because they contradict the reference residue, which is exactly why they must be visible rather than summarized.

PubMed (NCBI Entrez).version_or_build: No corpus version is exposed; the access date is the retrieval-version boundary (accessed 2026-08-10). Records are identified by PMID, and each retained record carries its own DOI where one exists.
PubMed (NCBI Entrez).license_or_terms: US Government work produced by the National Library of Medicine; PubMed records are in the public domain in the United States. Publisher abstracts are NOT public domain and are not retained - only identifiers, titles, journal, dates, citation and article_types.
PubMed (NCBI Entrez).retention_basis: Bibliographic metadata only, attributed to PubMed with DOI links. Used for two purposes: resolving durable identifiers for the Consensus results, and the article_types leg of the correction/retraction check, which is the only leg covering PMID:41673870.

corrections_and_retractions_checked: Yes, performed rather than argued, on three legs and covering every paper the packet cites in a claim. (1) Scite editorialNotices by DOI for SIX of them (accessed 2026-08-10) - PMID:41673870 is not in that index. (2) PubMed article_types for all seven. (3) PubMed CommentsCorrections links for all seven, which is the only leg that can see a correction or retraction published as a SEPARATE record: article_types leaves the original typed 'Journal Article' in that case, and since PubMed is the sole check for PMID:41673870 that was a real hole until this leg was added. All three legs are negative: no editorialNotices entry, no Retracted Publication or Erratum type, and zero CommentsCorrections links of any kind. PMID:41673870 published 2026-02-12, so absence of a notice still carries little information at this date; it is cited as one voice in a documented conflict and no conclusion turns on it. dbSNP separately reports rs1051266 as not merged. Per-record detail in raw/scite-and-pubmed-notices-2026-08-10.json and raw/pubmed-comments-corrections-2026-08-10.json.
privacy: No sample, genotype, or other personal data was read, transmitted or stored. The external requests are single-identifier metadata lookups plus one literature search on a public SNP; the local queries are read-only against a reference artifact.
